cards.title: Core idea
cards.body: A retry re-attempts a failed message, assuming the failure is temporary. A dead-letter queue (DLQ) is a separate queue or topic where a message goes after failing the maximum attempts, so a poison message stops blocking or wasting workers.

cards.title: How it works
cards.body: Retry a limited number of times, ideally with exponential backoff. RabbitMQ supports dead-letter exchanges natively; in Kafka you build retry and DLQ topics (orders, orders.retry, orders.dlq). The starter project runs Django with Kafka and RabbitMQ workers in Docker, with MAX_RETRIES per worker.

questions.q: Once failures go to the DLQ, is the problem handled?
questions.a: No. A DLQ only parks it. You need alerts on depth or age, a way to inspect, and a replay after the fix.
A message that always fails, which would otherwise block or waste workers forever.

questions.q: How is a DLQ built in Kafka?
questions.a: With separate retry and DLQ topics, such as orders.retry and orders.dlq.
